tagline: See every database on your local Postgres — its size, its owner, and which tables take up the space.
summary: My Local Postgres is a read-only inventory of the Homebrew Postgres cluster on your Mac. Every Luckee project creates its own database (`my_health`, `gmail_manager`, `code_control`, …); this app lists them all with size and owner so you can see what exists and what's growing.

Open a database to see its tables and other relations sorted by total size, including indexes and TOAST. The API connects to the maintenance database with one `DATABASE_URL` and reads only system catalogs — it never reads or changes your application data.
audience: You run many local projects that each create a Postgres database.
You want to know which databases exist and which ones are taking disk space.
You use Homebrew Postgres (or any local cluster you can reach with one connection string).
notFor: A SQL client or admin tool — no queries, edits, drops or backups.
Remote or managed databases (Supabase, RDS) — it's built for the local cluster.
Viewing row data — only sizes and names.

capabilities.title: Database list
capabilities.detail: `/` lists every database on the cluster with size and owner (`GET /api/databases`).

capabilities.title: Database detail
capabilities.detail: `/database-detail-page` lists relations by schema with total size (`GET /api/databases/:name/relations`).

capabilities.title: Safe catalog reads
capabilities.detail: Reads `pg_database` and `pg_class` only; per-database connections are short-lived and identifiers are never interpolated.

capabilities.title: Health without Postgres
capabilities.detail: `/api/health` keeps working when Postgres is down so you can tell the API from the database apart.

components.name: Web app
components.owns: Database list and detail tables. Calls `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`.

components.name: API
components.owns: A managed pool to the maintenance database (`DATABASE_URL`, default `postgres`) and catalog queries in `src/data/pg-catalog/`.
components.doesNotOwn: Any schema of its own — no migrations.

dataFlow: The API connects to `DATABASE_URL` (e.g. `postgresql://localhost:5432/postgres`) at startup.
Listing databases queries `pg_database` for name, owner and size.
Opening a database confirms the name exists, opens a short-lived connection to it and lists relation sizes from `pg_class`.
The web app renders both as tables.

trust.title: API (your machine)
trust.detail: Holds `DATABASE_URL`, which can usually see every database on the cluster. No auth — keep it on localhost.

commonTasks.title: Run it
steps: Run **Setup** in Hub (no database to create).
Set `DATABASE_URL=postgresql://<you>@127.0.0.1:5432/postgres` in the API's Environment step.
Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` on the web to the API's port.

commonTasks.title: Find what's using space
commonTasks.when: Disk is filling up or a project feels slow.
steps: Sort the database list by size.
Open the biggest one and look at the largest relations (often AI ledger or message tables).

troubleshooting.fix: Postgres isn't running or `DATABASE_URL` is wrong: `brew services start postgresql@16` and check the user name.
Your role may lack `CONNECT` on that database; connect as the database owner or a superuser.
`NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` defaults to 3009; Hub may run the API on 3066.

glossary.definition: The default `postgres` database the API connects to first.
A table, index, view or other object listed in `pg_class`.
Table plus its indexes and TOAST storage.

hubNotes: Useful alongside Hub's **Set up local database** flows — it shows which project databases actually exist.
The API defaults to port 3009 (shared with several projects); the registry says 3066.
